notes:
### 1. Individual Income Tax Rate(s)
* **Tax Rate:** Arizona imposes a single flat individual income tax rate of **2.5%** on taxable income for all filing statuses.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both **tax year 2025** and **tax year 2026** (unchanged; flat rate in effect since TY 2023).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Arizona Department of Revenue (ADOR) – Individual Income Tax Highlights: `https://azdor.gov/forms/individual-income-tax-highlights`
  * Arizona State Legislature – A.R.S. § 43-1011 (*Taxes and tax rates*): `https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/01011.htm`

---

### 2. Corporate Income and Franchise Tax
* **Corporate Income Tax Rate:** **4.9%** of Arizona taxable net income.
* **Minimum Tax:** The minimum corporate income tax is **$50** (the tax is the greater of $50 or 4.9% of net income).
* **Franchise Tax:** Arizona does not impose a corporate franchise tax.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both **tax year 2025** and **tax year 2026** (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Arizona Department of Revenue (ADOR) – Corporate Income Tax: `https://azdor.gov/business/corporate-income-tax`
  * Arizona State Legislature – A.R.S. § 43-1111 (*Tax rates for corporations*): `https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/01111.htm`

---

### 3. State Sales and Use Tax Rates & Local Jurisdictions
* **State Transaction Privilege Tax (TPT) / Sales Tax Rate:** Arizona imposes the Transaction Privilege Tax (TPT) on the business for the privilege of doing business in the state. For retail and most standard classifications, the total state rate is **5.6%**. This comprises:
  * Base statutory rate of **5.0%** (A.R.S. § 42-5010(A)), plus
  * An additional rate increment of **0.6%** (A.R.S. § 42-5010.01, effective through June 30, 2041).
* **State Use Tax Rate:** **5.6%** on the purchase price of tangible personal property stored, used, or consumed in Arizona (A.R.S. § 42-5155).
* **Local Jurisdictions:** Yes, local jurisdictions add rates on top of the state rate:
  * Arizona counties levy county excise and transportation taxes (e.g., A.R.S. § 42-6103, § 42-6105).
  * Cities and towns levy municipal privilege taxes under the Model City Tax Code (collected by ADOR).
  * Combined state, county, and city rates typically range between **5.6% and 11.2%**.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both **tax year 2025** and **tax year 2026** (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Arizona Department of Revenue (ADOR) – Tax Rate Table: `https://azdor.gov/transaction-privilege-tax/tax-rate-table`
  * Arizona State Legislature – A.R.S. § 42-5010 (*Rates; distribution base*): `https://www.azleg.gov/ars/42/05010.htm`
  * Arizona State Legislature – A.R.S. § 42-5010.01 (*Transaction privilege tax; additional rate increment*): `https://www.azleg.gov/ars/42/05010-01.htm`
  * Arizona State Legislature – A.R.S. § 42-5155 (*Levy of tax; tax rate; purchaser's liability*): `https://www.azleg.gov/ars/42/05155.htm`

---

### 4. Gross Receipts, Franchise, Margin, or Other Notable Business Taxes
* **Gross Receipts Tax:** Arizona does not levy a separate standalone general gross receipts tax; however, the **Transaction Privilege Tax (TPT)** is by statutory structure a gross receipts tax levied on the gross proceeds of sales or gross income across specific classifications (retail, restaurants, commercial lease, contracting, utilities, etc.).
* **Franchise / Margin / Capital Stock Tax:** Arizona does not levy a franchise tax, gross margin tax, or capital stock tax.
* **Pass-Through Entity (PTE) Tax:** Eligible partnerships and S corporations can elect an entity-level income tax at a rate of **2.5%** (matching the individual income tax rate) under A.R.S. § 43-1014.
* **Applicability:** Applies to both **tax year 2025** and **tax year 2026** (unchanged).
* **Official Sources:**
  * Arizona Department of Revenue (ADOR) – TPT Information: `https://azdor.gov/transaction-privilege-tax`
  * Arizona State Legislature – A.R.S. § 42-5008 (*Levy of tax; purposes; distribution*): `https://www.azleg.gov/ars/42/05008.htm`
  * Arizona State Legislature – A.R.S. § 43-1014 (*Entity-level tax election; partnerships; S corporations*): `https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/01014.htm`

notes:
### 1. Individual Return Due Dates and Extension Rules
* **Due Date (Calendar-Year Filers):** Calendar-year individual income tax returns are due on or before April 15 following the close of the calendar year.
* **Extension Rules:** 
  * Under A.R.S. § 42-1107, Arizona grants an automatic 6-month extension to file (to October 15). 
  * If a federal extension (Form 4868) is granted, the taxpayer is deemed granted the same 6-month Arizona extension without submitting a separate state form (check the extension box on the return). Taxpayers not filing a federal extension, or needing to make an extension payment by paper, file Arizona Form 204 by April 15.
  * An extension extends the time to file, not to pay. At least 90% of the tax liability must be paid by the original due date to avoid the extension underpayment penalty of 0.5% per 30-day period (capped at 25%).
* **Applicability:** Applies to tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URLs:** 
  * https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/00325.htm
  * https://www.azleg.gov/ars/42/01107.htm
  * https://azdor.gov/

---

### 2. Corporate and Pass-Through Return Due Dates and Extension Rules
* **C-Corporations (Form 120):**
  * **Due Date:** Calendar-year returns are due on or before April 15 (the 15th day of the 4th month following the close of the taxable year).
  * **Extension:** 6-month extension (to October 15) using Arizona Form 120/165EXT or an approved federal Form 7004. At least 90% of the tax liability must be paid by the original due date.
* **Partnerships (Form 165):**
  * **Due Date:** Calendar-year returns are due on or before March 15 (the 15th day of the 3rd month following the close of the taxable year) per A.R.S. § 43-325(3).
  * **Extension:** 6-month extension (to September 15) using Arizona Form 120/165EXT or an approved federal Form 7004.
* **S-Corporations (Form 120S):**
  * **Due Date:** Calendar-year returns are due on or before March 15 (the 15th day of the 3rd month following the close of the taxable year), conforming with federal S-corporation deadlines.
  * **Extension:** 6-month extension (to September 15) using Arizona Form 120/165EXT or an approved federal Form 7004.
* **Applicability:** Applies to tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URLs:** 
  * https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/00325.htm
  * https://www.azleg.gov/ars/42/01107.htm
  * https://azdor.gov/

---

### 3. Elective Pass-Through Entity (PTE) Tax
* **Existence:** Yes, codified at A.R.S. § 43-1014.
* **Tax Rate:** The tax rate is equal to the individual income tax rate prescribed in A.R.S. § 43-1011, which is a flat 2.5%.
* **How and When to Elect:**
  * The partners or shareholders of a partnership or S corporation consent to be taxed at the entity level.
  * The election must be made annually on or before the due date or extended due date of the entity's return.
  * The election is made by checking the PTE election box on the timely filed return (Form 165 for partnerships or Form 120S for S corporations).
* **Applicability:** Applies to tax years 2025 and 2026 (the rate remains 2.5%).
* **Official URLs:** 
  * https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/01014.htm
  * https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/01011.htm
  * https://azdor.gov/

---

### 4. Composite / Group Nonresident Returns for Pass-Through Entities
* **Availability & Rules:** 
  * Arizona permits partnerships and S corporations to file a composite return on behalf of qualifying nonresident individual owners under ADOR Individual Income Tax Ruling ITR 16-2.
  * **Participation Requirement:** A minimum of 10 participating eligible nonresident individuals is required.
  * **Return Used:** Arizona Form 140NR (Nonresident Personal Income Tax Return), designated as a composite return.
  * **Restrictions:** Participating members cannot claim itemized deductions (only standard deductions are allowed), tax credits, or net operating loss carryovers.
  * **Estimated Payments:** If voluntary composite estimated payments are made, the entity files Form 140ES using the entity's EIN (not Form 120/165ES).
* **Applicability:** Applies to tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official URLs:** 
  * https://azdor.gov/
  * https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/01091.htm

---

### 5. Estimated Tax Payment Requirements and Nonresident Withholding
* **Estimated Tax Requirements:**
  * **Individuals (A.R.S. § 43-581):** Required if Arizona gross income for the taxable year exceeds $75,000 ($150,000 for married filing joint) and was greater than $75,000 ($150,000 joint) in the preceding year. Combined estimated payments and withholding must equal at least 90% of current year tax or 100% of preceding year tax. Due in four installments: April 15, June 15, September 15, and January 15.
  * **Corporations (A.R.S. § 43-582):** Required if Arizona corporate tax liability is $1,000 or more. (Mandatory electronic payments via EFT apply if liability is $500 or more).
  * **Electing PTEs (A.R.S. § 43-1014(B)(3)):** Must pay estimated tax pursuant to A.R.S. § 43-581 as necessary. Paid electronically via AZTaxes.gov or using voucher Form 120/165ES.
* **Pass-Through Nonresident Withholding:**
  * **Rule:** Not found in Arizona statutes. Arizona does not impose a mandatory withholding requirement on pass-through entities with respect to distributive share/income allocations to nonresident partners or shareholders. Nonresident compliance is handled via individual Form 140NR, a composite return, or entity-level taxation under A.R.S. § 43-1014.
* **Applicability:** Applies to tax years 2025 and 2026 (unchanged).
* **Official URLs:** 
  * https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/00581.htm
  * https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/00582.htm
  * https://www.azleg.gov/ars/43/01014.htm

---

### 6. Main Return Forms
* **Individual Forms:**
  * **Form 140:** Resident Personal Income Tax Return
  * **Form 140PY:** Part-Year Resident Personal Income Tax Return
  * **Form 140NR:** Nonresident Personal Income Tax Return (also used for composite returns)
  * **Form 140-SBI / 140PY-SBI / 140NR-SBI:** Small Business Income tax returns (if electing to report small business income separately)
  * **Form 204:** Application for Filing Extension (Individuals)
  * **Form 140ES:** Individual Estimated Tax Payment Voucher
* **Corporate Forms:**
  * **Form 120:** Corporation Income Tax Return
  * **Form 120A:** Corporation Income Tax Return - Short Form
  * **Form 120/165EXT:** Application for Extension of Time to File Corporate or Partnership Returns
  * **Form 120ES / 120/165ES:** Corporation Estimated Tax Payment Voucher
* **Pass-Through Entity Forms:**
  * **Form 165:** Partnership Income Tax Return (includes Schedule K-1 and Schedule K-1(NR))
  * **Form 120S:** S Corporation Income Tax Return (includes Schedule K-1 and Schedule K-1(NR))
  * **Form 120/165EXT:** Application for Extension of Time to File
  * **Form 120/165ES:** Estimated Tax Payment Voucher for Partnerships and S Corporations (used for PTET)
* **Applicability:** Applies to tax years 2025 and 2026.
* **Official URL:** 
  * https://azdor.gov/
